He is also the solo developer of PolyBall, a free rhythm arcade game for Android, browser and desktop in which every catch plays a note. This site holds his portfolio, his CV, the PolyBall pages and his 3D printing write-ups.

- He is open to software engineering roles.

## Abdallah El Belkasy

> Software engineer in Dubai. He designs systems, plans the build and ships them. At Odoo he turns what a business needs into a data model and a delivery plan, then builds it in Python and PostgreSQL. On his own he designed, built and released the rhythm game PolyBall, and he wrote the Rust control plane for E-Jam, an open-source test bench for network switches.

Markdown copy of [abdaishere.com](https://abdaishere.com/). His friends call him AbdA.

### In short

- Based in Dubai, UAE (UTC+4). Speaks Arabic (native) and English (fluent).
- Software Engineer at Odoo in Dubai, on enterprise client projects, April 2025 to present.
- B.Sc. in Computers and Artificial Intelligence, Cairo University, 2019 to 2023. GPA 3.5 out of 4.0, Excellent with Honours.
- Open to software engineering roles.
- Main languages: Python, SQL, Rust, JavaScript, Dart and GDScript. University coursework in C++ and Java.

### Work

#### Odoo (April 2025 to present)

Software Engineer on enterprise client projects in Dubai, for clients across the Gulf. He works directly with each client's team, maps what the business needs onto standard features, puts the rest into a data model and a delivery plan, and builds it in Python and PostgreSQL: business logic, integrations, database fixes and performance work, on more than 100 projects. He works mainly in stock and accounting, and sometimes in point of sale, e-commerce and HR. He designed and built a stock aging layer: aging data is stored per stock move and updated on every move, with a function that rebuilds everything, so a report that walked the whole stock list on every render now renders in under a second. He worked on the billing system for a third-party logistics client, the biggest system he has worked on, with a postpaid model (storage and every handling service calculated at release) and a prepaid model (rented floor area). He is now building an integration with two external systems, about 150 hours of work, and a multi-step approval system. He reviews partner developers' code against Odoo's development standards, has coached two partners and is involved in certifying partners to work with Odoo. Star of the Month, July 2026.

Daily stack: Python, PostgreSQL, the Odoo ORM, JavaScript (OWL), XML and QWeb, REST integrations.

#### PolyBall (2026)

A rhythm arcade game he designed, coded, scored and released alone, in Godot 4 and GDScript. It is live on Google Play (since 13 November 2026) and also on itch.io, GameJolt and the web. There were 19 tagged releases between 23 September and 13 November 2026.

The engineering behind it:

- An audio engine that synthesises every note at runtime with 16 instruments, up to 12 notes at once. The game ships no music files.
- Continuous integration on GitHub Actions across six build targets, and gameplay bots that play 24 runs per pass with deliberate mistakes.
- 15 locales, with Arabic right-to-left layout covered by automated tests.
- A leaderboard backend on Supabase (PostgreSQL) with a monthly cup, server-side anti-cheat (score ceilings and run-code checks), a name filter, and block and report: 11 SQL migrations with automated tests.

- Game page: https://abdaishere.com/polyball/
- Play in the browser: https://abdaishere.com/polyball/play/
- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.polyball.game

#### E-Jam (2023)

A distributed test bench that runs the RFC 2544 and RFC 2889 benchmarks on network switches. It was his Cairo University graduation project, built by a team of five developers in collaboration with Siemens EDA, whose engineers were the mentors, sponsor and product owner. It was a university project, not a job at Siemens.

His part: Center Point, the control plane, written in Rust on Actix Web. It is a REST API that drives every stream, device and process through explicit state machines and publishes to Apache Kafka with Avro schemas from a schema registry. He also built the Flutter admin client that configures tests and charts results live. He is the top contributor to the repository with 256 commits. The project is open source under the MIT licence.

- Case study: https://abdaishere.com/e-jam/
- Source: https://github.com/Abdaishere/E-Jam

### How he works

- Design: start from what the business or the player needs, map it onto what already exists, and put only the gap into a data model before any code.
- Plan: make the wrong state impossible to reach. E-Jam's control plane moves every stream, device and process through an explicit state machine.
- Ship: make releasing routine. PolyBall went out as 19 tagged releases in under two months, with CI across six build targets and gameplay bots that play 24 runs per pass.
- Check: measure the thing itself. See the note on the silent web build below.

## PolyBall

> Every note you hear, you played. PolyBall is a free one-thumb arcade game where you spin a ring so the falling ball lands on its own colour. Every catch plays a note, so each run writes its own song. One miss ends the run.

Markdown copy of [abdaishere.com/polyball](https://abdaishere.com/polyball/). Write the name as PolyBall: one word, capital P and B. On Google Play it is listed as "PolyBall: Color Spin Arcade".

### How it plays

A ball drops onto a spinning polygon split into coloured segments. Turn the ring so the ball lands on its own colour. Each catch scores, builds your combo and speeds things up. Land on the wrong colour and the run is over.

The ring can have anything from 3 sides to 63, and every shape keeps its own best score.

### You are the band

PolyBall ships with no music files at all. Every sound comes from how you play.

- Every catch is a note. Each colour is a note of the chord underneath, so everything you play lands in key.
- Keep your streak going and the band joins in: first the bass, then the arpeggio, then the lead.
- Hit Fever and the whole screen turns gold.
- One miss and it all stops. Then you tap play again, because that song was getting good.

### Five ways to play

- Classic: the pure loop. Endless, and it only gets faster.
- Remix: Classic, plus a new twist every ten catches. Each stage ends on a boss ball.
- Music: perform the song. Balls land on the beat.
- Time: beat the clock. Clean catches buy back seconds.
- Zen: no clock, no score, and no way to lose.

There is also a daily run (one attempt per day, the same for everyone) and a global leaderboard with a monthly cup.

### Where to play

It is free everywhere.

- Android, on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.polyball.game
- In your browser, nothing to install: https://abdaishere.com/polyball/play/
- Windows, Mac and Linux downloads: https://abdaishere.com/polyball/#get
- itch.io: https://abdaishere.itch.io
- iPhone and iPad are coming later. The browser version works there today.

### Fair play

- Free to play. Ads sit between runs, never during one.
- Nothing you buy changes your rank. Purchases are Remove Ads, a starter pack, gems or coins, which buy cosmetics and Combo Shields. Any run that a shield or an ad revive touched is marked assisted and never reaches the leaderboard. Nothing random is sold for money.
- Plays offline. The leaderboard catches up when you are back online.
- No account, no sign-up, no email. Pick a name or keep the one the game gives you.
- Colour-blind mode stamps a distinct shape on every colour.
- 15 languages: English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Russian, Turkish, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Arabic (Egyptian and Modern Standard), Hindi and Indonesian. Arabic is laid out right to left.

### Who made it

PolyBall is made by one person, Abdallah El Belkasy, a software engineer in Dubai: design, code, audio and release. Current version: 0.10.11. Live on Google Play since 13 November 2026.

### How it is built

- Engine: Godot 4, GDScript.
- Sound: a synthesiser inside the game with 16 instruments, up to 12 notes at once. Colour is mapped to chord degree across an eight-bar progression, and bass, arpeggio and lead are performed note by note on a swung grid.
- Testing: continuous integration on GitHub Actions across six build targets. Bots play 24 runs per pass and miss on purpose, so the numbers look like a real player's.
- Leaderboard: Supabase (PostgreSQL). The server gives each run a code and holds a score ceiling, filters names, and lets players block or report. 11 SQL migrations with automated tests.

## E-Jam

> E-Jam is an open-source distributed test bench for network switches. It runs the RFC 2544 and RFC 2889 benchmarks. Abdallah El Belkasy wrote its Rust control plane and its Flutter admin client.

Markdown copy of [abdaishere.com/e-jam](https://abdaishere.com/e-jam/).

### What it is

A switch has to prove it can carry full traffic without dropping or delaying packets. The proof is a standard set of measurements at several frame sizes, each repeated many times. E-Jam spreads that work across as many machines as you give it. On each one, C++ generators fire traffic at the switch and verifiers check what comes back out, every process in its own container. Their statistics stream home over Apache Kafka, typed against a schema registry, and the client charts them while the test is still running.

### Context

- Cairo University graduation project, 2022 to 2023 (his work on it: January to August 2023).
- Built in collaboration with Siemens EDA, whose engineers were the mentors, the sponsor and the product owner. It was a university project, not employment at Siemens.
- Team of five developers.
- Open source under the MIT licence: https://github.com/Abdaishere/E-Jam

### Abdallah's part

- Center Point, the control plane: a Rust service on Actix Web whose REST API drives streams, devices and processes through explicit state machines and publishes to Apache Kafka with Avro schemas from a schema registry.
- The Flutter admin client that configures tests and charts results live.
- Top contributor to the repository, with 256 commits.

The C++ packet generators and verifiers were written by his teammates.

### Stack

Rust, Actix Web, Apache Kafka, Avro, C++, Dart, Flutter, Docker (the Kafka stack runs from Docker Compose).

### Links

- Case study with diagrams: https://abdaishere.com/e-jam/
- Source on GitHub: https://github.com/Abdaishere/E-Jam
- Video walkthrough: https://youtu.be/oPZLR4RM150
